answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall at the quartz boundary of compute. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random memory indices; failure to return data matching the plume-like entropy of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. This willow-bound latency constraint ensures that each agent maintains a unique, non-shared bus access, preventing pooling. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain their status, whereas fakes incur costs scaling linearly per identity.
